answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network maps interaction graphs across a topological cut, verifying sparse boundaries like a narrow canyon between clusters. Multi-agent committees audit suspicious clusters; if collusive subgraphs cross this threshold, automated stake slashing imposes superlinear attacker cost scaling with identity count. Auditing nodes expand verification past the horizon of local clusters, rooting trust anchors in a robust tree topology as resilient as ancient juniper.
